GEMARA: Rava asked Rav Naḥman: What is the halakha with regard to wages for a worker who does not have anything to eat? Is it permitted to provide a poor worker with work on the intermediate days of the Festival? Rav Naḥman said to him: We learned this in the mishna: Or to provide for the needs of the seller, if he has nothing to eat. What is added by mentioning the condition that he has nothing to eat? Does it not add the case of wages and not only the case of one selling items he owns? Rava said to him: No, it is merely explaining what is meant by the needs of the seller.

Abaye raised an objection from a mishna (18b): Promissory notes may not be written on the intermediate days of a Festival, but if the lender does not trust the borrower and is concerned that without such a note he will be unable to collect, or if he has nothing to eat, he may write a promissory note. The Gemara elaborates: What is added here by the words: If he has nothing to eat? Are they not meant to add that a promissory note may be written for the sake of the wages of the scribe who draws up the document? Conclude from it that it is permitted to hire a worker who is in need of a livelihood even for work that would otherwise be prohibited on the intermediate days of a Festival.

Rav Sheshet raised an objection from a mishna (Pesaḥim 55a) that addresses the prohibition against performing labor on the eve of Passover: And the Rabbis say: The practitioners of only three crafts are permitted to perform labor until midday on Passover eve, and they are the tailors, the barbers, and the launderers, whose work is needed for the Festival. The baraita elaborates: The tailors may perform labor on Passover eve, as a layperson is permitted to sew in his usual manner during the intermediate days of the Festival. Since similar labor is permitted during the Festival, one may be lenient on Passover eve as well. The barbers and the launderers are permitted to work, as those who arrive from overseas or one who leaves prison are permitted to cut their hair and wash their clothes on the intermediate days of the Festival because they had no opportunity to do so prior to the Festival.

And if it enters your mind that paying wages to a worker who does not have anything to eat is permitted on the intermediate days of the Festival, then all other types of labor should also be permitted on the eve of Passover, as there is something similar permitted on the intermediate days of the Festival, namely, the wages paid to a worker who does not have anything to eat. Tailors are permitted to work on the eve of Passover because similar work is permitted during the intermediate days of the Festival. The payment of wages to a worker who does not have anything to eat on the Festival must be prohibited, as otherwise similar work, i.e., any work involving the payment of wages, would be permitted on the eve of Passover, which is not the case.

Rav Pappa strongly objects to this: If that is so, that one can derive halakhot in this manner, then building as well should be permitted on the eve of Passover, as a wall that tilts toward the public domain and is likely to fall may be demolished and rebuilt in the usual manner on the intermediate days of a Festival due to the danger posed to passersby. Since building under such circumstances is permitted on the intermediate days of a Festival, it should be permitted in general on the eve of Passover.

Ravina also strongly objects to this: If that is so, a scribe [lavlar] who draws up documents should be permitted to do so on the eve of Passover, as one may write betrothal deeds, bills of divorce, and receipts on the intermediate days of a Festival.

Rather, Rav Ashi said that Rav Sheshet’s original objection has no basis: Are you raising a contradiction between the halakhot of the intermediate days of a Festival and the halakhot of the fourteenth day of Nisan, i.e., the eve of Passover? They are not comparable, as the prohibition against labor on each is for a different reason: Labor is prohibited on the intermediate days of a Festival because it involves excessive exertion, and in a situation of significant loss the Sages permitted it. In contrast, the prohibition against labor on the fourteenth of Nisan is due to the need to prepare for the Festival, and especially the Paschal lamb. Whatever is needed for the Festival, e.g., the work of tailors and barbers, the Sages permitted, but whatever is not needed for the Festival, the Sages did not permit.
he: גְּמָ׳ בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא מֵרַב נַחְמָן: שְׂכַר פְּעוּלָּה שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל, מַהוּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ, תְּנֵינָא: אוֹ לְצוֹרֶךְ הַמּוֹכֵר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל. לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לָאו לְאֵתוֹיֵי שְׂכַר פְּעוּלָּה! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, פָּרוֹשֵׁי קָא מְפָרֵשׁ.

אֵיתִיבֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אֵין כּוֹתְבִין שְׁטָרֵי חוֹב בַּמּוֹעֵד, וְאִם אֵינוֹ מַאֲמִינוֹ, אוֹ שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל — הֲרֵי זֶה יִכְתּוֹב. שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל — לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי? לָאו לְאֵתוֹיֵי שְׂכַר פְּעוּלָּה! שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.

מוֹתֵיב רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, שָׁלֹשׁ אוּמָּנִיּוֹת עוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה בְּעַרְבֵי פְסָחִים עַד חֲצוֹת: הַחַיָּיטִין וְהַסַּפָּרִין וְהַכּוֹבְסִין. הַחַיָּיטִין — שֶׁכֵּן הֶדְיוֹט תּוֹפֵר כְּדַרְכּוֹ בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד, הַסַּפָּרִין וְהַכּוֹבְסִין — שֶׁכֵּן הַבָּאִין מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם וְהַיּוֹצֵא מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִין מוּתָּרִין לְסַפֵּר וּלְכַבֵּס בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד.
וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ שְׂכַר פְּעוּלָּה שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל שְׁרֵי — כׇּל מְלָאכוֹת נָמֵי לִישְׁתְּרוֹ, דְּהָא אִיכָּא שְׂכַר פְּעוּלָּה שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מַה יֹּאכַל!
מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה בִּנְיָן לִישְׁתְּרֵי, שֶׁכֵּן כּוֹתֶל הַגּוֹהֶה לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים — סוֹתֵר וּבוֹנֶה כְּדַרְכּוֹ מִפְּנֵי הַסַּכָּנָה!
מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רָבִינָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה לַבְלָר לִישְׁתְּרֵי, שֶׁכֵּן כּוֹתְבִין קִידּוּשֵׁי נָשִׁים גִּיטִּין וְשׁוֹבָרִין!

אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מוֹעֵד אַאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר קָא רָמֵית? מוֹעֵד — מִשּׁוּם טִירְחָא הוּא, וּבִמְקוֹם פְּסֵידָא שָׁרוּ רַבָּנַן. אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר — מִשּׁוּם צוֹרֶךְ יוֹם טוֹב הוּא. מִידֵּי דְּצוֹרֶךְ יוֹם טוֹב שָׁרוּ רַבָּנַן, מִידֵּי דְּלָאו צוֹרֶךְ יוֹם טוֹב לָא שָׁרוּ רַבָּנַן.

en: It was stated in the mishna that the Rabbis say: The practitioners of only three crafts are permitted to perform labor until midday on Passover eve. It was taught in explanation of their opinion: The tailors may perform labor on Passover eve, as a layperson is permitted to sew in his usual manner during the intermediate days of the Festival. Since this type of labor is permitted during the intermediate days, when the prohibition against labor is more stringent than on Passover eve, one may be lenient on Passover eve as well. Barbers and launderers, may perform labor on Passover eve, as one who arrives from a country overseas or one who leaves prison who did not have time to cut their hair or launder their clothing before the Festival may cut their hair and wash their clothing on the intermediate days of the Festival. Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says: Shoemakers may also perform their labor, because Festival pilgrims may repair their shoes during the intermediate days of the Festival.

The Gemara asks: With regard to what principle do the Rabbis and Rabbi Yosei disagree? The Gemara answers: One Sage, Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, holds: We learn the halakha with regard to the initiation of labor from the halakha with regard to the conclusion of labor; if it is permitted to repair shoes, it is also permitted to initiate their production. And one Sage, the Rabbis, holds: We cannot learn the halakha with regard to the initiation of labor from the halakha with regard to the conclusion of labor; therefore, although it is permitted to repair shoes, it is prohibited to produce new ones.
he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים שָׁלֹשׁ אוּמָּנִיּוֹת. תָּנָא: הַחַיָּיטִין, שֶׁכֵּן הֶדְיוֹט תּוֹפֵר כְּדַרְכּוֹ בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד. הַסַּפָּרִין וְהַכּוֹבְסִין, שֶׁכֵּן הַבָּא מִמְּדִינַת הַיָּם וְהַיּוֹצֵא מִבֵּית הָאֲסוּרִין מְסַפְּרִין וּמְכַבְּסִין בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף הָרַצְעָנִין, שֶׁכֵּן עוֹלֵי רְגָלִים מְתַקְּנִין מִנְעָלֵיהֶן בְּחוּלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד.
בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי? מָר סָבַר: לְמֵידִין תְּחִילַּת מְלָאכָה מִסּוֹף מְלָאכָה, וּמַר סָבַר: אֵין לְמֵידִין תְּחִילַּת מְלָאכָה מִסּוֹף מְלָאכָה.

sections.en: The mishna continues: A layman, who is not a skilled tailor, may sew in his usual manner if necessary for the Festival, whereas a craftsman may form only temporary stitches. And one may interweave the cords attached to the frames of beds upon which a mattress is placed. Rabbi Yosei says: One may only tighten the cords but not interweave them.
sections.he: הַהֶדְיוֹט תּוֹפֵר כְּדַרְכּוֹ, וְהָאֻמָּן מַכְלִיב. וּמְסָרְגִין אֶת הַמִּטּוֹת. רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, אַף מְמַתְּחִין:

en: בְּקִיעַ I m. (בקע; compare בִּצְעָה) fissure, ditch, especially small pond for washing clothes. Moʿed Katan 8ᵇ נברכת וב׳, explained as גיהא ובר גיהא a large pond and a small pond. Tosefta Bava Batra I, 2. Ib. Moʿed Katan I, 9 זו היא נ׳ … ב׳ Nibrekheth and B’kia are the same; Yerushalmi ib. I, 80ᵈ כל שהוא תושב וכ׳ any permanent cut in the ground is called בקיע (fissure, a grave, wash-pond &c.). [Another opinion in Arukh ב׳ = אבן ב׳ a flat stone whereon washers beat their clothes; Yerushalmi l. common gender. כל שהוא וכ׳ any stone fixed in the ground is called a b’kia.—Manuscript Munich and ed. Venice נְקִיעַ, see נֶקַע.]

כָּבַשׁ (Biblical Hebrew; compare כָּבַס)
1) to press, squeeze. Oholot VIII, 5 כ׳ את האבן וכ׳ if one pressed a stone on (weighted) the sheet. Beitzah 23ᵇ שהיא כּוֹבֶשֶׁת because it (the wagon) presses (the ground) down. Shabbat XX, 5 לא כוֹבְשִׁין you must not screw down, see מַכְבֵּשׁ; and from—Part. pass. כָּבוּשׁ, f. כְּבוּשָׁה pressed, compressed; pressing. Ib. 135ᵃ; Tosefta ib. XV (XVI), 9; and e. ערלה כ׳ היא the foreskin (which seems to be wanting) is pressed (to the membrum). Tosefta Oholot IX, 4 כאילו אבנים כְּבוּשׁוֹת וכ׳ as if stones were placed tightly upon them. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 15 ההר … כְּבוּשִׁין על וכ׳ a mountain on each side pressing upon (preventing the run of) the springs; and from

—2) כ׳ פנים (בקרקע) to press the face into the ground, to hide one’s self in fear or shame. Sanhedrin 19ᵇ כָּבְשׁוּ פניהם בקרקע they cast their looks down (were afraid to give an opinion). Yerushalmi ib. X, 27ᵈ (reference. to Isaiah VII, 3) א"ת כובס אלא כּוֹבֵשׁ שהיה כובש פניו וכ׳ read not kobes, but kobesh
, for he hid his face and fled before him; (Bavli ib. 104ᵃ דכבשינהו לאפי Chald.).—3) to press vegetables, meat &c.; to preserve, pickle. Toharot II, 1 האשה … כּוֹבֶשֶׁת וכ׳ if a woman was pressing vegetables in a pot. 'Uktzin II, 1 זתים שכְּבָשָׁן וכ׳ olives which one pressed with their leaves; and from—Part. pass. כָּבוּשׁ preserved substance, pickle. Chullin 97ᵇ, and from כ׳ הרי הוא כמבושל preserved substances are in ritual law like cooked.—plural כְּבוּשִׁין. Pesachim II, 6. Yerushalmi Shabbat I, 3ᶜ bottom of page כְּבוּשֵׁיהֶן preserves made by gentiles; and from

—4) Transferred to store, hide. Chagigah 13ᵃ (reference. to Mishlei XXVII, 26) א"ת כבשים אלא כְּבוּשִׁים Manuscript Munich (missing in ed.; see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note) read not K’basim (sheep) but K’bushim (hidden things), see כִּבְשָׁן; Yalkut Mishlei 961.—Sotah 10ᵇ; Makkot 23ᵇ (reference. to Breishit XXXVIII, 25) יצאת … ממני יצאו כבושים a divine voice went forth and said, ‘from me went forth the secret things’ (I declare that Judah is the father of Tamar’s children; Arukh: ממני היו הדברים כ׳, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 6); Yalkut Breishit 145; YalkutSam. 112., see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 6); Yalkut Breishit 145; YalkutSam. 112. to detain (compare עצר). Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Bayom, p. 193ᵇ; כָּבְשָׁה אותם מטרונא וכ׳ the matron detained them one day longer; כבשה אותן התורה וכ׳ the Law detained them one day longer (before the Lord); ib. 195ᵃ, sq.; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. supplement to Pesikta Rabbathi, section (Parashah) 4. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 8, end האיש כּוֹבֵשׁ וכ׳ the man detains his wife from going out; and e.

—6) to suppress, restrain, conquer. Sanhedrin XI, 5 (89ᵃ) הכּוֹבֵש את נבואתו (a prophet) who suppresses his prophecy (being afraid to proclaim it). Pirkei Avot IV, 1 הכיבש את יצרו who conquers his passion. Eicha Rabbah to V, 1 כובש את הגדול (not כביש), see זַרְזִיר I. Yerushalmi Sukkah V, 55ᵇ top עד שאתה מְכַבֵּשׁ … בוא וכְבוֹש וכ׳ instead of conquering the barbarians, come and subdue the Jews; Eicha Rabbah to I, 16; ib. to IV, 19. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 25 הוא כוֹבְשׁוֹ וכ׳ he suppresses (withholds the evidence) and does not produce it.—כ׳ עון to suppress guilt, to forgive, cause forgiveness. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Eth Korb., p. 61ᵇ; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 16, see כֶּבֶשׁ; and from

—7) to violate. Esther Rabbah to VII, 7 [read:] הרי הוא כּוֹבְשֵׁנִי וכ׳ behold, he is attacking me in thy presence.

—8) to pave, grade a road.—Part. pass. כָּבוּשׁ, f. כְּבוּשָׁה. Midrash Tanḥuma Chukat 20 דרך כ׳ a graded road; ib. ed. Bub. 47; Yalkut Bamidbar 764. [Pirké d’R. El. Chaldaic LII כובשים במזלות, read with Yalkut Joshua 22: חושבים; Yalkut Breishit 77 רוגשים.]

Piël - כִּיבֵּשׁ
1) to press, squeeze.—Part. pass. מְכוּבָּשׁ, plural מְכוּבָּשִׁים. Tosefta Mikvaot VI (VII), 17 לכלוכי צואה … המ׳ (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) והמכושים, correct accordingly) secretory substances … which are compressed, i.e. dried up by being sat upon.

—2) (compare סָלַל II) to press down, make even, grade. Beitzah IV, 5 מְכַבְּשִׁין you may press the ashes down (make a graded surface for baking); and e.—Transferred to level, make plain. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to I, 2 (play on כבשים, Mishlei XXVIII, 26, see כֶּבֶשׁ) … כְּבָשִׁים … תהי׳ מְכַבֵּשׁ לפניהם וכ׳ it may be read K’bashim (grades), as long as thy pupils are young, make the words of the Law plain before them; when they are older reveal to them the secrets (reasons) of the Law; Yalkut ib. 985 הֱיֵה כוֹבֵשׁ לפניהם (another explained, see infra).—כ׳ את הריחיים [to carve steps for the grain,] to put the millstones in working order. Moʿed Katan I, 9; explained ib. 10ᵃ to sharpen the millstones (see נָקַר I), (oth. opinion) to cut the hole out for the hopper.

—3) (interch. with Kal) to conquer, defeat. Yerushalmi Peah VII, 20ᶜ top שבע שכִּיבְּשׁוּ seven years during which they were engaged in conquering the land; Chullin 17ᵃ שכבשו. Sifré Devarim 51 לכַבֵּש ח"ל עד שלא יְכַבְּשׁוּ וכ׳ to conquer foreign land before they shall have conquered Palestine. Pesachim 5ᵇ נכרי שכִּיבַּשְׁתּוֹ a gentile who is in thy power. Yevamot 65ᵇ (reference. to וכבשה, Breishit I, 28) איש דרכו לכַבֵּשׁ וכ׳ it is man who conquers (the earth) but not woman; Kiddushin 35ᵃ; and from

—4) to suppress, withhold. Shir HaShirim Rabbah l. common gender. תהי׳ מכבש לפניהם וכ׳ withhold from them, i.e. teach them merely the words of the Law without arguments; (another explained, see supra).

—5) (denominative of כֶּבֶשׁ) to storm, climb over. Tosefta Sotah VI, 6 מכבש את הגנות וכ׳ climbing over the garden fences and violating the women; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 53; Yalkut Breishit 94 מַכְבִּישׁ Hifil

Nifal - נִכְבַּשׁ
1) to be pressed down, suppressed. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Eth. Korb. p. 61ᵇ כל דבר שהוא נ׳ סופו לצוף whatever is pressed down, is liable to come to the surface again; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 16.

—2) to be submissive. Midrash Till. to Psalms XXX, end when scholars sit down ונִכְבָּשִׁין אלו לאלו and are submissive (respectful) to one another; (Shabbat 63ᵃ ונוחין).

—3) to have surreptitious intercourse. Sifra Emor, Parah 6, Chaldaic V נ׳ עם; Yevamot VII, 5 נ׳ על.

Hifil - הִכְבִּישׁ to climb, see supra.

Hithpaël - הִתְכַּבֵּשׁ,

Nithpaël - נִתְכַּבֵּשׁ to be conquered, be taken. Yerushalmi Sheviit VI, 36ᶜ bottom of page כמי שנִתְכַּבְּשׁוּ they are to be treated as if they had been subdued (in the days of Joshua). Ib. שמא נִתְכַּבְּשָׁה מד"ת perhaps it was to be taken by the command of the Law; Yerushalmi Yevamot VII, 8ᵃ bottom of page (correct accordingly). Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 18 עכשיו … מִתְכַּבֶּשֶׁת בידו just now Jerusalem may be taken by him (Sennacherib). [Pesik. Zutr., Ekeb, ed. Bub. p. 30 מתכבשים, מתכבשות, see כָּתַשׁ.]

sections.en: One may set up an oven, a stove, and a mill on the intermediate days of a Festival. Rabbi Yehuda says: One may not chisel millstones for the first time on the intermediate days of a Festival.
sections.he: מַעֲמִידִין תַּנּוּר וְכִירַיִם וְרֵחַיִם בַּמּוֹעֵד. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר, אֵין מְכַבְּשִׁין אֶת הָרֵחַיִם בַּתְּחִלָּה:

en: מַחֲלָץ m. , du. מַחֲלָצַיִם, plural מַחֲלָצִין (חָלַץ, compare חָלִיץ) a sort of windlass, loops of a rope attached to a heavy slab for rolling over plastered roofing &c., see מַעֲגִילָה. Makkot 9ᵇ עד שישמט מַחֲלָצוֹ מידו Variant in Arukh section (Parashah) see מחצל (ed. מחצלו) until the entire ramming machine slips out of his hands (opposed to נפסק the breaking of the rope); Yerushalmi ib. II, beginning 31ᶜ עד שיתיר את כל המחלצין (read שיפיל or שיוריד) until he lets go all the loops (explained = נפסק החבל). Ib. מה דמר ר"י בשמיטת המ׳ (not המחלצון) what R. J. says (‘until he drops the whole rope’) refers to the slipping of the machine; Tosefta ib. II, 3 ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) עד שיפול כל המחצלין מידו (read: שיפיל … המחלצ׳). Moʿed Katan I, 10 (11ᵃ) שפין את … אבל לא במחלצים (Yerushalmi ed. … צַיִים; Manuscript Munich מחצלים) you may plaster over cracks in the roof, or roll them over with a (small) roller, using the hands or the feet, but not with the windlass, see Yerushalmi ib. 81ᵃ top.—[The Variant lect. מחצל־ rests upon a popular transposition, as if from מָחַץ. The interpretation of מחצל by commentators as trowel does not fit the context.]

מַנְעוּל m. (Biblical Hebrew; נָעַל) lock. Bava Batra 65ᵇ; Tosefta ib. III, 1 את הנגר ואת המ׳ the bolt (fastened to the wall) and the lock (fastened to the door), opposed to מפתח the portable key. Moʿed Katan I, 10. Zavim IV, 3; and from—Transferred the lock of the buttock, anus. Kohelet Rabbah to III, 19; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 17 (some ed. מַנְעָל); Yalkut Kohelet 969 מנעל; see אֱפִיפְּיוֹן.

מַעֲגִילָה f. (עָגַל)
1) roller, a slab for rolling over a plastered roof, see מַחֲלָץ. Makkot II, 1; Tosefta ib. II, 3; Yerushalmi ib. II, beginning 31ᶜ. Moʿed Katan I, 10 במ׳ ביד וברגל, explained ib. 11ᵃ כעין מ׳ וכ׳ with hands and feet as with a roller.

—2) a press for straightening wood. Sifré Devarim 308, see כּוּן Piël; Yalkut ib. 942 מַעֲגָלָה.

מַעֲקֶה m. (Biblical Hebrew; עקה to restrain) railing. Moʿed Katan I, 10. Sifré Devarim 229 פטור מן המ׳ not subject to the law &c. (Devarim XXII, 8). Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia VIII, 2, see קוּפָּה; and e.—בֵּית מַ׳ proper noun of a place Beth-Maʿăkeh. Yerushalmi Ma'aser Sheni IV, 54ᵈ bottom of page, see מְשַׁח III.

צִנּוֹר, צִינּוֹר m. (Biblical Hebrew; צנר, enlargement of צור, compare צִינוֹק, טִינָּר, סִינָר &c.) [anything carved out or turned,]
1) socket in which the door-pivot turns, or pivot. Moʿed Katan I, 10 (11ᵃ) הציר והצ׳ the pivot and the socket (or the socket and the pivot; see Rashi in Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 30).

—2) water pipe, spout, duct. Mikvaot IV, 1 המניח כלים תחת הצ׳ if one puts vessels under the spout (which feeds a bath). Pirkei Avot Zar. 75ᵃ; Tosefta ib. VIII (IX), 3 תחת הצ׳ … מקלחין under the spout when its waters splash forth; Yerushalmi ib. V, end, 45ᵇ. Mikvaot IV, 3, see חָטַט. Tosefta Eruvin IX (VI), 22 (larger than מזחילה). Ib. 23 צ׳ המקלח לרשות וכ׳ a gutter which runs into a public road whether containing water or wine; and from—Euphem. vagina. Pirké d’R. El. Chaldaic XVI.—plural צִנּוֹרוֹת, צִינּ׳. Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. III, 42ᶜ top, see מָשַׁךְ. Tosefta Shabbat VII (VIII), 16; Berakhot 50ᵇ, see מָשַׁךְ. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 42 (reference. to Breishit XIV, 3) [read:] לא היה שם ים אלא צ׳ היאורים וכ׳ there was no lake there at the time, but (afterwards) the pipes of the ducts (the water veins in the rocks) burst, and a lake was formed (with reference. to Job XXVIII, 10); Yalkut ib. 72 צורות היאור (correct accordingly).

שׁוּף II
1) to smooth, rub, polish, sharpen; to smear over, plaster. Kelim XIV, 5 משיְשׁוּפֶינּוּ (Mishnah ed. משישׁוּפֶנּוּ; Arukh משיְשַׁפֶּנּוּ, from שָׁפָה I) a sword becomes susceptible of uncleanness when it is furbished. Ib. XVI, 1 משיְשׁוּפם בעור הדג when he smooths them by rubbing with the skin of a fish; Sanhedrin 20ᵇ; Nedarim 56ᵇ משיְשַׁפֵּם (Rashi משישופם). Kelim l. common gender. גמר שלא לָשׁוּף if he decided not to smooth them. Yerushalmi Berakhot III, 5ᵈ bottom of page לאיזה דבר הוא שָׁפָהּ for what purpose should he polish it? Chullin 25ᵃ, sq.; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia II, 10. Tosefta Toharot VI, 12 ושָׁפָה את רוקו and she rubbed his spittle off (with her foot); שָׁפוֹת וכ׳ (להיות) … שכן for it is the habit of Israelitish women during menstruation to rub off &c. Yerushalmi Shabbat VII, 10ᵇ top רוקק ושָׁף he spits on the stone pavement and rubs it out (with his foot). Moʿed Katan I, 10 שָׁפִין את הסדקין you may plaster over the rifts in the roof (during the festive week). Shabbat XX, 3 ולא שפין אותן nor must you rub them (with the hand to cleanse them). Eduy. I, 8 שורין ושפין וכ׳ you must observe levitical cleanness when you soak them and rub (your body) with them. Shabbat 75ᵇ השף בין העמודים he who rubs (smooths skins) between columns; Yerushalmi ib. VII, 10ᶜ bottom of page השף את העור על גבי העמוד. Kelim XXX, 1 שָׁפָן בשופין files them with a file. Pesachim II, 7 אבל שָׁפָה היא וכ׳ but she may rub (the bran) dry over her body (to soften her skin); and from

—2) to run smoothly, glide. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 6; Midrash Samuel Chaldaic IX.

—3) (Biblical Hebrew) to grind, crush, stamp. Sifré Devarim 315 שיהו חטים שָׁפוֹת זו וכ׳ that wheat grains rub against one another and drop &c., see סֹלֶת; Yalkut ib. 944.—Midrash Till. to Psalms IV, 7 וישראל … ואתם באים לָשׁוּף אותה מן העקב and the Israelites say to them (the gentiles asking for a share in the hereafter), in how many troubles … we surrendered our lives for the sanctification of the Lord, and you want to stamp it (all this good) out of your heels (out of the ground)?; (ed. Bub. אותם על העקב, correct accordingly); Yalkut ib. 627 לשוף עצמיכם מן העקב (correct accordingly).—[Midrash Till. to Psalms XCII וישופני עקב, see שׁוּף I.]

Nifal - נִישּׁוֹף
1) to be rubbed off, made smooth, level. Tosefta Bava Kamma X, 4 מטבע ונ׳ if he took by force a coin, and it became rubbed off (effaced).

—2) to be ground, crushed. Tosefta Bava Metzia XI, 8 מוציא אדם זבלו … כדי שיִישּׁוֹף וכ׳ a man may take out his material for dung and place it in front of his house, that it may be stamped upon by the feet of man and beast; Bava Kamma 30ᵃ; 81ᵇ; Bava Metzia 118ᵇ כדי שיהא נישוף. Bava Kamma 28ᵇ נשוף באבן (Manuscript Florence ונושף, read: נִישָּׁף) was smashed against a stone; (Yerushalmi ib. III, 3ᶜ top נחבט).—V. שָׁפַף.

sections.en: One may construct a railing for a roof or a balcony if it is done in a nonprofessional manner, as the work of a layman, but not if it is done skillfully, as the work of a craftsman. One may plaster the cracks in an oven and roll over them with a roller, a wooden tool used to smooth out clay, with a hand or a foot, but not with a presser, a tool that is specially designed for this task. With regard to the hinge of a door, and the cylinder of the hinge, and the cross beam that holds the door, and a lock and a key that broke, one may fix them on the intermediate days of a Festival as these items are essential for the Festival and their repair cannot be delayed. This is permitted, provided that he does not intend ahead of time to do his labor on the Festival and delay it until that time. And with regard to all preserved food from which one can eat on the Festival, since they become ready to be eaten in a short amount of time, he may preserve them on the intermediate days of a Festival.
sections.he: עוֹשִׂין מַעֲקֶה לְגַג וּלְמִרְפֶּסֶת מַעֲשֵׂה הֶדְיוֹט, אֲבָל לֹא מַעֲשֵׂה אֻמָּן. שָׁפִין אֶת הַסְּדָקִין וּמַעְגִּילִין אוֹתָן בַּמַּעְגִּילָה בַּיָּד וּבָרֶגֶל, אֲבָל לֹא בַמַּחֲלָצָיִם. הַצִּיר וְהַצִּנּוֹר וְהַקּוֹרָה וְהַמַּנְעוּל וְהַמַּפְתֵּחַ שֶׁנִּשְׁבְּרוּ, מְתַקְּנָן בַּמּוֹעֵד, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְכַוֵּן מְלַאכְתּוֹ בַּמּוֹעֵד, וְכָל כְּבָשִׁין שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לֶאֱכֹל מֵהֶן בַּמּוֹעֵד, כּוֹבְשָׁן:
